answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring every agent to stake a small copper-backed deposit before joining a shared work reef: the stake stays locked while peers attest real completed jobs. At the nadir of trust, a brand-new identity with no history may only take tiny low-value tasks, so spinning up thousands of fake identities costs far more in locked deposits and waiting time than any reward they could extract, while honest agents gradually earn bigger jobs as their attested record grows.
